newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Snubbing heady gains on Wall Street on Wednesday night, South African shares drooped in futures-led activity on Thursday. Gold shares were further pressured by bullion which hovered weakly below the $350 level.
"The market was led by the nose by futures traders," a dealer said. "It looked as if they were unwinding baskets."
Traders said industrial stocks were given a respite early in the afternoon when buying interest, from both local players and offshore, materialised.

However, most of these gains were erased towards the close with the industrial 100 percent index ending 48.4 points weaker at 7,962.6. The March industrial futures contract was also well down at 7,728/7,737 from 7,810 settlement on Wednesday.
Traders said rand-hedge stocks, including Sasol and Richemont, felt the brunt of the sell-off by futures players.

Although the rand ended slightly weaker against the dollar on Thursday, the unit has made strong gains since the beginning of the month when it was hovering above the 4.70 level as exporters have rushed to cover open short positions.
The rand finished Thursday at 4.5645 bid from a 4.5595 overnight close.
Rand-hedge stocks generally come into favour when the local unit weakens against offshore currencies, but they lose their lustre when the rand strengthens.
Sasol shed 200 cents or 3.8 percent to 51.25, Richemont fell 75 cents to 62.50 rand and Minorco lost 25 cents to 104.50 rand.
Amongst other stocks Premier added six cents to 626 cents but Nedcor lost 125 cents 67.50 rand.
An improved rand continued to be the thorn in the flesh of gold stocks, also good rand-hedges, with the gold index losing almost 1.5 percent on a sickly bullion price.
"No one tends to believe a sudden rise in the gold price unless it is followed through," a dealer said referring to a spike in the metal price to above the $356 level earlier this week.
Bullion was last trading at $349.10/349.60 an ounce.
The all gold 100 index lost 19.8 points to 1,365.7 as Dries lost 110 cents to 42.30 rand and Vaal Reefs shed 700 cents to 309 rand. But Freegold bucked the trend adding 25 cents to 33 rand.
The all gold share futures contract was last at 958/960 from 976.

Traders said they expected a firmer market on Friday with sentiment boosted by a better performance on the rand and bond markets. However, market direction was dependent on the actions of futures players.
"With these futures guys, one just doesn't know," one dealer said.
The overall market index ended 29.3 points down at 6,658.2 with the related March futures contract at 6,042/6,050 from 6,128.
